name: Vivaldi
businessModel: Search-engine partnerships and sponsored default bookmarks/speed dials; no user data selling, no AI upsell
license: Proprietary UI on Chromium (BSD); UI source viewable but not open-licensed

version.upstream: Chromium 152 ESR with security backports from Chromium 156

updateCadence: Major every ~2-4 months, frequent minor security updates; snapshot 4190.x already on Chromium 156 for 8.3
pitch: The most customizable Chromium browser, with built-in mail, notes and no AI.
summary: Chromium-based browser with deep UI, tab, gesture and command customization plus built-in mail, calendar, feeds and notes. Publicly pledges to stay AI-free. Lost MV2 (uBlock Origin) with Chromium 152 in 2026.
bestFor: Power users who want to tweak everything
People who want a browser with zero AI features
Users who want built-in mail, calendar and RSS
notFor: Anyone who needs full uBlock Origin (MV2 is gone)
People who want a fully open-source browser
Beginners who find lots of options overwhelming

pros.title: Deepest customization
pros.detail: Themes, layouts (6 presets in 8.0), toolbars, gestures, quick commands and per-site settings go further than any other mainstream browser.

pros.title: Best-in-class tab tools
pros.detail: Vertical tabs, tab stacks, tiling, workspaces and hibernation are all built in.

pros.title: No AI, by pledge
pros.detail: Vivaldi publicly committed in August 2025 to keep AI features out of the browser.

pros.title: Built-in productivity suite
pros.detail: Mail, calendar, feeds, notes, translate, capture and reading list ship in the box.

pros.title: Desktop-class Android extensions
pros.detail: Since 8.2 (Sept 2026) Android can install Chrome Web Store extensions (MV3 only).

cons.title: MV2 and uBlock Origin gone
cons.detail: Snapshot 4116.3 moved to Chromium 152 and dropped MV2; only uBlock Origin Lite and the built-in blocker remain.

cons.title: Not fully open source
cons.detail: Chromium parts are open, but the Vivaldi UI is source-viewable only.

cons.title: Heavy and complex
cons.detail: Uses more RAM than Safari or Firefox and the settings depth can overwhelm newcomers.

cons.title: No fingerprint protection
cons.detail: Blocks trackers but offers no dedicated fingerprinting resistance.

signatureFeatures: Built-in Mail, Calendar and Feed reader

faq.a: No. Vivaldi has pledged to keep AI features out and 8.0 added none.

faq.q: Does uBlock Origin still work in Vivaldi?
faq.a: Not in 8.2: Chromium 152 removed MV2 support. Use the built-in blocker or uBlock Origin Lite.

faq.q: Can I install extensions on Vivaldi for Android?
faq.a: Yes, since Vivaldi 8.2 (Sept 2026) you can add Chrome Web Store extensions; only MV3 extensions work.

timeline.event: Public pledge to keep AI out of Vivaldi
Vivaldi 8.0: Unified design and layout presets
Snapshot on Chromium 152 loses MV2 support
Vivaldi 8.2: Chrome Web Store extensions on Android
Minor update 14 backports Chromium 156 security fixes

switching.note: Imports from Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Opera, Safari and others; Chrome extensions install from the Chrome Web Store.

sync.note: Vivaldi account with optional separate encryption password; extensions do not sync

passwordManager.note: Built-in manager with sync; no breach check

mv2.note: MV2 lost when Vivaldi moved to Chromium 152 (snapshot 4116.3, July 2026); Android extensions are MV3 only

privacy.defaults: Built-in tracker and ad blocker, Google services stripped; no fingerprint protection
privacy.telemetry: Anonymous usage statistics, can be disabled

spec.patchLag: Backports Chromium security fixes within days (e.g. 8.2 minor update 14 on Oct 29 carries Chromium 156 fixes)

notes: Chrome Web Store extensions (MV3) since 8.2, Sept 2026
Extensions in private tabs added in 8.2 minor update 4

jsSpeed: Chromium V8 engine, same class as Chrome
pageLoad: Blink rendering; extra UI layer adds slight overhead
networkSpeed: Chromium network stack with HTTP/3 and preloading
startup: Heavier UI than Chrome means slower cold start
smoothness: Blink compositor; busy UI can add jank
memory: Chromium multi-process model plus Vivaldi UI overhead
cpu: Chromium baseline, UI adds some load
battery: Chromium baseline; Energy saver mode available
resourceControls: Tab hibernation and memory saver, fewer controls than Brave/Chrome
privacyDefaults: Built-in tracker blocker, Google services stripped
blocking: Built-in blocker with custom lists, but no full uBlock Origin now
fingerprinting: No dedicated fingerprint resistance beyond Chromium
patchSpeed: Backports Chromium fixes within days (minor update 14 on Oct 29)
telemetry: Anonymous stats only, opt-out, Norwegian company
lookCustom: Unified UI with 6 layout presets and 7,000+ themes
advancedSettings: Huge settings tree plus Chromium flags
tabManagement: Stacks, tiling, vertical tabs and workspaces
searchFreedom: Nicknames, search in address bar, unlimited engines
downloads: Dedicated download panel with sort and open options
productivity: Notes, panels, capture, Quick Commands, reading list
extras: Mail, calendar, feeds, notes, capture, Panic mode
extensions: Chrome Web Store but MV2 gone since July 2026
sync: Encrypted sync of most data; extensions do not sync
passwords: Built-in manager with sync, no breach check
mobileApps: Android and iOS apps; Android has extensions since 8.2
webCompat: Chromium engine on desktop and Android
accessibility: Chromium a11y with extra keyboard options
openSource: Chromium open, Vivaldi UI source-viewable only
businessTrust: Independent, no AI, transparent privacy stance
longevity: Ten years old, steady release cadence
